nodes.label: Pavement lines and symbols separate traffic lanes and indicate permitted passing, lane changes and turning use.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: This fact summarizes marking functions; no accepted peer gives an opposing function list. Specific markings are retained separately.

nodes.label: Pavement markings can designate pedestrian crossings and the stopping position for a sign or signal.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: This fact identifies what crosswalk and stop-position markings designate. The accepted action rules are separate, not competing designation rules.

nodes.label: A continuous line beside the roadway identifies its edge.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: A continuous road-edge line marks the edge; a solid white line between lanes calls for staying put except in a special circumstance. Location is part of the distinction.

nodes.label: White lane lines separate streams of traffic moving the same way.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: White lines separate same-direction traffic; yellow lines separate opposing traffic. Keep direction with the color.

nodes.label: A broken white lane line allows a lane change after checking that the movement is safe.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: A broken white line allows a safe lane change; solid white generally calls for remaining in the lane with a stated special-circumstance qualification.

nodes.label: A solid white lane line calls for staying in the lane unless a special circumstance requires a change.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: A continuous road-edge line marks the edge; a solid white line between lanes calls for staying put except in a special circumstance. Location is part of the distinction.
A broken white line allows a safe lane change; solid white generally calls for remaining in the lane with a stated special-circumstance qualification.

nodes.label: For a stop required by a sign or signal, stop before the vehicle reaches the stop line or crosswalk.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: A crosswalk identifies the place where pedestrians cross the road.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Drivers must yield to pedestrians already in a crosswalk or about to step into it.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: A pedestrian crossing can exist even without painted crosswalk markings.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Yellow lane lines separate vehicles moving toward each other.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: White lines separate same-direction traffic; yellow lines separate opposing traffic. Keep direction with the color.

nodes.label: A broken yellow center line permits passing when the maneuver is safe.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: With a paired solid and broken yellow center line, a driver on the solid-line side may not pass.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: With a paired solid and broken yellow center line, a driver beside the broken line may pass when safe.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: A double solid yellow center line prohibits passing from either side.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: A driver may cross a solid yellow line to enter a driveway when the turn is safe.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: A reversible lane carries traffic in opposite directions at different times.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: Reversible lanes change the direction of travel at different times; a shared center lane serves specified turns from either direction. Do not treat a turning lane as an unrestricted travel lane.

nodes.label: Reversible lanes are commonly marked by paired broken yellow lines.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: Paired broken yellow lines commonly mark reversible lanes; a shared middle lane has solid-and-broken yellow lines on each side. Keep the marking patterns distinct.

nodes.label: Before entering a reversible lane, check the current lane-use signs or signals.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: Reversible-lane entry requires checking current controls; some shared middle lanes can become reversible at peak times and require checking availability and safety. Preserve both contexts.

nodes.label: A green overhead arrow permits use of the lane directly below it.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: The overhead green arrow permits lane use, while the overhead red X prohibits it. Do not confuse the lane-use indication with an ordinary intersection light.

nodes.label: A red overhead X prohibits driving in the lane below it.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: The overhead green arrow permits lane use, while the overhead red X prohibits it. Do not confuse the lane-use indication with an ordinary intersection light.

nodes.label: A flashing yellow overhead X limits the lane to turning.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: A flashing yellow overhead X limits use to turning; a steady yellow overhead X warns of a change and calls for leaving as soon as safe.

nodes.label: A steady yellow overhead X warns of a lane-use change and calls for leaving the lane as soon as safe.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: A flashing yellow overhead X limits use to turning; a steady yellow overhead X warns of a change and calls for leaving as soon as safe.

nodes.label: A reserved lane is identified by signs describing the permitted use and often by a white diamond.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: A lane labeled Transit or Bus is reserved for buses.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: A lane labeled Bicycle is reserved for bicycle travel.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: HOV means high-occupancy vehicles and identifies a lane for vehicles carrying more than one person.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: The sign for an HOV lane specifies the required occupancy and the days and hours of the restriction.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: An HOV three sign requires at least three occupants in the vehicle.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: A shared center lane is reserved for left turns and permitted U-turns, and vehicles from either direction may use it for those turns.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: Reversible lanes change the direction of travel at different times; a shared center lane serves specified turns from either direction. Do not treat a turning lane as an unrestricted travel lane.

nodes.label: Alternating left-turn arrows show the movements permitted from a shared middle lane.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: A shared middle lane is bounded on each side by a solid yellow line paired with a broken yellow line.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: Paired broken yellow lines commonly mark reversible lanes; a shared middle lane has solid-and-broken yellow lines on each side. Keep the marking patterns distinct.

nodes.label: Some shared middle lanes become reversible during peak traffic periods, so entry requires checking that the lane is available and safe.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: Reversible-lane entry requires checking current controls; some shared middle lanes can become reversible at peak times and require checking availability and safety. Preserve both contexts.

nodes.label: When signs and markings do not assign lane use, general driving, passing and turning rules determine the lane to use.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.
